title: Rex Stewart as idol and learning off records
summary: Roy and friends copied Red Nichols records; trumpeter Archie Johnson and Rex Stewart, who stayed at the house and showed him breaks, shaped him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: then. Because I... We just...a couple of other little cats I knew, we were playing around, you know. We'd be taking things off the records, like Red Nichols. Because I wasn't exposed to Louis Armstrong then, you know. Or Bix. It was Rex then, and Red Nichols, you know.

Well, actually, what got me started was the trumpet player that was in my brother's band, a ...(?)... named Archie Johnson. He was a killer, man, you know. Then Rex came and stayed at our house, and he showed me a couple of breaks. Man, he was really my idol. I mean, like I couldn't... I didn't dig it because I didn't get fat like he was, you know, so I could look like him. I started to do everything he did, you know. When he came in with Fletcher, he got me and took me, and he set behind me and he's showing what he's reading and all these parts, you know. And all his mannerisms that he was... It was for me, you know.
